messages:
Priya: FYI created a new cloud account for the EMEA research cluster (redwood-emea-research). We need quota bumps before we can onboard Dedicated nodes and private endpoints.
Maya: Cool — what exact quotas do you need?
Priya: Short list: p4d.24xlarge (GPU) desired initial quota 10 -> we currently have 1.
Priya: NLB target group targets per AZ to 2000 (we expect ~1.6k targets during scaleouts).
Priya: Interface endpoints (com.amazonaws.eu-west-1.ec2/vpc endpoints): 80 -> current 20.
Priya: ENI / elastic network interface limit per account also likely needs bump to support the GPU fleet.
Tom: Also call out target registration rate limit — we see registration bursts from autoscaling that need ~400-500 registrations/sec for short windows.
Ben: Do you have justification for AWS? They usually ask for traffic/capacity numbers.
Priya: Yes. Dedicated cluster planned: 20 p4d nodes initially, scale to 40 in six weeks. Each node registers 48 targets across services (model pods + metrics). We expect occasional churn when rolling images -> hence high registration rate.
Maya: Can you paste a quick asks text so I can file the support case?
Priya: Adding template below I will open the case but would appreciate someone from platform to review before submit.
Priya: ```
Hello,
We're requesting quota increases for account a-1234567890 (redwood-emea-research) in eu-west-1 with the following justifications:
- EC2 G-type (p4d.24xlarge): increase from 1 to 10 to support Dedicated inference cluster for production workloads. Initial usage plan: 20 nodes by week 1, scale to 40 in 6 weeks. Each node runs latency-sensitive model endpoints.
- Network Load Balancer (NLB) target group targets per Availability Zone: increase to 2000 to support target registration surge during rolling deploys and autoscaling.
- VPC interface endpoints (com.amazonaws.eu-west-1.*): increase from 20 to 80 to support per-subnet private control-plane connectivity for telemetry, model registry, and KMS access.
- Elastic Network Interfaces (ENI): bump account and per-AZ soft limits to accommodate peak pod density for GPU instances and interface endpoints.
- Target registration rate: please allow burst registration up to 500 registrations/sec for short windows (<= 5 minutes) for our autoscaling and deploy patterns.
Justification: Redwood Inference will run Dedicated inference capacity for enterprise customers in eu-west-1. These increases are required to meet our SLA for latency and to avoid throttling during rolling deploys. We can provide traffic charts and forecast numbers on request.
Thank you,
Priya (infra)
```
SRE Oncall: Throwing in an immediate mitigation suggestion: add more, smaller target groups and stagger registration across AZs to spread the load until quotas are approved. Also enable fallback to a smaller model variant via routing policy if registration fails.
Tom: Good call. We'll prepare a short runbook to stagger registration (scripted delays) if AWS says no.
Lina (finance): Heads-up: if AWS approves p4d quota, estimated monthly cost at our current pricing is ~225k USD/month for 10 p4d nodes. We should confirm budget owner for the pilot and whether we want reserved commitments instead.
Ben: Can we start with a partial quota (e.g., 4 p4d) to test and then request the rest later? AWS sometimes approves incremental increases faster.
Priya: Yep, we asked for 10 but noted we can accept progressive increases. Will mark in the case.
Cloud Support Bot: Case opened: 1234567890. Current status: pending internal review. Assigned to support engineer: Rajesh.
Priya: Copy of the case note (added additional CPU/GPU utilization forecasts and autoscaler churn graphs to the case attachment).
Maya: Rajesh asked for a network diagram and peak registration timestamps — uploaded both.
Cloud Support Bot: Support update: support engineer requests confirmation of account owner and contact email for validation.
Priya: Contact for validation: priya@redwood.ai. Please set case to high (production onboarding).
SRE Oncall: Once quotas are in, we should validate by spinning up a staged fleet and running a synthetic registration test (script included in infra repo under infra/qa/target-regression-test). If quotas not approved, we'll run staggered registration and enable temporary traffic shaping at the LB.
Ben: Assigned action: Maya/Tom to review the case text and network diagram by EOD. Lina to confirm provisional budget for pilot. Priya to follow up with AWS if no response in 48 hours.
Priya: Thanks all — will ping again with updates from Rajesh. :thumbsup:
